questions.title: Dual Comparison Principle: Centre and Spread

parts.text: State the two essential statistical components required for a complete comparison between two distributions in a Cambridge exam, and give one example statistic for each component.

questions.title: Interpreting Median and IQR in Context

parts.text:
Two groups of commuters, $A$ and $B$, have journey times summarized as follows:
- Group $A$: $\text{Median} = 42\text{ minutes},\; \text{IQR} = 18\text{ minutes}$
- Group $B$: $\text{Median} = 50\text{ minutes},\; \text{IQR} = 10\text{ minutes}$

State which group generally has longer journey times, and state which group has more consistent journey times, giving statistical justifications.

questions.title: Choosing Between Mean and Median with an Outlier

parts.text:
The waiting times, in minutes, of 7 patients are:
$$12,\; 13,\; 14,\; 15,\; 16,\; 17,\; 58$$
State whether the mean or median is more appropriate for describing the typical waiting time, and give a specific reason.

questions.title: Mean and Standard Deviation in Context: Times

parts.text:
Two delivery teams have their completion times, in minutes, summarized as follows:
- Team North: $\text{Mean} = 72\text{ minutes},\; \text{Standard deviation} = 6\text{ minutes}$
- Team South: $\text{Mean} = 68\text{ minutes},\; \text{Standard deviation} = 11\text{ minutes}$

Compare their delivery times in terms of speed and consistency.

questions.title: Effect of Data Corrections on Grouped Frequency Estimates

parts.text: A grouped frequency table includes the class $40 < x \le 50$. A recorded observation of $42$ is corrected to $44$. State and explain whether the estimated mean calculated from the grouped table will change.

In the same grouped frequency table with consecutive classes $40 < x \le 50$ and $50 < x \le 60$, an observation originally recorded as $49$ is corrected to $51$. State and explain whether the estimated mean calculated from the grouped table will change.

questions.title: Comparing Parcel Masses from Five-Number Summaries

parts.text:
Two delivery depots, Red and Blue, record the masses, in kg, of parcels. The five-number summaries are:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Depot} & \text{Minimum} & Q_1 & \text{Median} & Q_3 & \text{Maximum} \\ \hline \text{Red} & 20 & 30 & 42 & 50 & 60 \\ \text{Blue} & 24 & 34 & 46 & 52 & 58 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Calculate the IQR and range of parcel masses for both depots.
Make two comparisons between the parcel masses of Red Depot and Blue Depot in context.

questions.title: Comparing Plant Heights across Two Orchards

parts.text:
The heights, in cm, of apple trees in two orchards have summaries:
- Orchard $A$: $\text{Minimum} = 20,\; Q_1 = 28,\; \text{Median} = 35,\; Q_3 = 44,\; \text{Maximum} = 60$
- Orchard $B$: $\text{Minimum} = 18,\; Q_1 = 30,\; \text{Median} = 40,\; Q_3 = 46,\; \text{Maximum} = 52$

Calculate the interquartile range for each orchard.
Make two distinct contextual comparisons between the tree heights in Orchard $A$ and Orchard $B$, referencing both central tendency and spread.

questions.title: Raw Data: Comparing Two Sports Teams (Falcons vs Lynx)

parts.text:
The ordered finishing times, in minutes, for 8 runners in team Falcons are:
$$74,\; 78,\; 81,\; 83,\; 86,\; 90,\; 92,\; 97$$
Find the median, $Q_1$, and $Q_3$, and hence calculate the IQR for the Falcons.

The ordered times for team Lynx are: $76,\; 79,\; 82,\; 85,\; 87,\; 88,\; 91,\; 94$ minutes, giving $\text{Median} = 86.0\text{ minutes}$ and $\text{IQR} = 9.0\text{ minutes}$.
Compare the race performances of the Falcons and the Lynx with respect to:
(i) average speed,
(ii) consistency,
(iii) overall race outcome.

questions.title: Comparing Exam Marks from Cumulative Frequency Curves

parts.text:
Quartile readings obtained from cumulative frequency graphs of examination marks for two schools are:
- School $X$: $Q_1 = 42,\; \text{Median} = 56,\; Q_3 = 68$
- School $Y$: $Q_1 = 48,\; \text{Median} = 60,\; Q_3 = 66$

Calculate the interquartile range for each school and state which school has a higher proportion of students scoring below 60 marks.
Write a complete comparative report on the performance of School $X$ and School $Y$, discussing central tendency, spread, and the shape/skewness of each distribution.

questions.title: Delivery Times with an Extreme Delay: Outlier Analysis

parts.text:
The delivery times, in minutes, for 7 parcels dispatched by a courier are:
$$18,\; 19,\; 20,\; 20,\; 21,\; 22,\; 96$$
Calculate the mean and median delivery times, and state the mode.
Explain which measure of central tendency (mean, median, or mode) best represents a typical delivery time for this courier, and explain the numerical discrepancy between the mean and the median.

questions.title: Comprehensive Cumulative Frequency Comparison: 200 Applicants across Two Test Centres

parts.text:
Two testing centres, East and West, each tested $N = 200$ applicants. Cumulative frequency curves produced the following readings:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline & Q_1 & \text{Median} & Q_3 \\ \hline \text{East} & 34 & 52 & 66 \\ \text{West} & 42 & 54 & 62 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Calculate the interquartile range for both centres.

The pass mark for the test is set at $50$ marks. From the curves, the cumulative frequency at $50$ marks is $90$ for East and $76$ for West.
(i) Find the number of applicants who passed at each centre.
(ii) State which centre achieved a higher pass rate, giving the percentages.

Compare the performance of applicants at East Centre and West Centre with respect to:
(i) central tendency (median score),
(ii) consistency (interquartile range),
(iii) skewness and the distribution of scores.

questions.title: Comprehensive Synthesis: Quality Assurance, Extreme Values, and Linear Coding of Mean and Variance

parts.text:
A manufacturing plant inspects the diameters, $x\text{ mm}$, of 10 cylindrical bearings. The summary statistics are:
$$\sum (x - 20) = 4.2,\quad \sum (x - 20)^2 = 3.68$$
Calculate the mean and the standard deviation of the diameters $x$.

A competitor produces bearings with diameter summary:
$$\text{Minimum} = 19.4,\; Q_1 = 20.1,\; \text{Median} = 20.4,\; Q_3 = 20.7,\; \text{Maximum} = 21.8$$
(i) Calculate the IQR and range for the competitor's bearings.
(ii) Determine whether either the minimum ($19.4\text{ mm}$) or the maximum ($21.8\text{ mm}$) is an outlier under the $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ rule.

Explain why comparing the competitor's dataset with the plant's dataset is more robustly conducted using the median and IQR rather than the mean and standard deviation, and evaluate which producer demonstrates greater consistency.
